knowledge_point.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=8 \\ 4x-7y &=13.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 8 \\ 4 & -7 & 13\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 8 \\ 4 & -7 & 13\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & -7 & 13\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=4 \\ y &=-3,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-3$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-3)=4\,⇒\,x=-2.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-2$ and $y=-3.$
